iti śrutvā vacastasya ṣoḍaśābdāṃtare gate ..

3.3.m: Hearing his words, when an interval of sixteen years had passed, / he marched to Kurukṣetra with an army of one hundred and twenty-five thousand.

mahīrājasutāñjitvā samāhūya mahāvatīm ..

3.3.m: Having conquered the sons of Mahīrāja, he summoned Mahāvatī; / sending forth the king and plundering his wealth,

3.3.s:
liṃgārthaṃ kṛtavānyatnaṃ sa nṛpaḥ kīrtisāgare ..
na prāptassa nṛpastaṃ vai svagehāya tadā yayau ..242..

लिंगार्थं कृतवान्यत्नं स नृपः कीर्तिसागरे ॥
न प्राप्तस्स नृपस्तं वै स्वगेहाय तदा ययौ ॥242॥
3.3.m: that king made an effort to obtain the liṅga in Kīrtisāgara; / not obtaining it, that king then went to his own home.

lakṣacaṃḍīṃ kārayitvā paramānaṃdamāptavān..
jayacaṃdrastu tacchrutvā putraśokasamanvitaḥ .. 243 ..

3.3.m: Having caused the Lakṣacaṇḍī [ritual] to be performed, he attained supreme joy. / But Jayacandra, hearing that, was overcome with grief for his son;

3.3.s:
nirāhāro yatirbhūtvā mṛtaḥ svargapuraṃ yayau ..
sahoḍḍīnena sa nṛpaḥ kṛtvā yuddhaṃ bhayaṃkaram .. 244 ..

निराहारो यतिर्भूत्वा मृतः स्वर्गपुरं ययौ ॥
सहोड्डीनेन स नृपः कृत्वा युद्धं भयंकरम् ॥ 244 ॥
3.3.m: fasting and becoming an ascetic, he died and went to the city of heaven. / That king, having fought a dreadful battle with Sahoḍḍīna,

3.3.s:
saptāhorātramātreṇa mleccharājavaśaṃ gataḥ ..
mārito bahuyatnena mahīrājo na vai mṛtaḥ .. 245 ..

सप्ताहोरात्रमात्रेण म्लेच्छराजवशं गतः ॥
मारितो बहुयत्नेन महीराजो न वै मृतः ॥ 245 ॥
3.3.m: fell under the sway of the Mleccha king in just seven days and nights. / Though Mahīrāja was subjected to being killed with great effort, he did not die.

jyotirūpasthitaṃ tatra caṃdrabhaṭṭo nṛpājñayā ..

क्षुरप्रेण च बाणेन हत्वा वह्नौ ददाह वै ॥ 246 ॥
3.3.m: Then the Mleccha Sahoḍḍīna bound him fast. / Candrabhaṭṭa, by order of the king, slew with a crescent-shaped arrow / him who stood there in the form of light, and burned him in fire.

3.3.m:
That Mleccha, seizing Vidyunmālā and much wealth, / installed his own servant Kutukoḍḍīna there and departed.
1 [Page] 281. Description by Sūta to Śaunaka and others of historical events occurring around the twelfth century from the time of the reign of Vikrama. Therein: Description introducing the account of the re-incarnation of the Kauravas, Yādavas, Pāṇḍavas, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and others who had died previously in the Bhārata War. Verses: 34.
2 [Page] 282. Description of the division of the eighteen royal territories located in the land of Bharata and so forth; the defeat of the Śakas by Śālivāhana, the grandson of Vikramāditya, after the devastation of the Aryan realm was wrought by the Śaka kings; the fixing of the boundary between the Aryan and Mleccha lands; the installation of Sāmasiṃha in the Mleccha realm by the Son of God; the ascent of Śālivāhana to heaven after ruling for sixty years. Verses: 34.

3.3.m:
3 [page] 283: An account of the reigns of kings born in the lineage of Śālivāhana; an account of the expedition of world conquest by King Bhoja, the tenth king from Śālivāhana; the dialogue of King Bhoja with Śiva residing in the country of Vāhīka; the slaying of the Vāhīka by Kālidāsa through the power of a sacrifice to Caṇḍī; an account of the establishment of the Āryan religion by King Bhoja, the Muḥammadan religion, and the state of the place of Sāmasiṃha; the period of King Bhoja: 32 verses.
4 [page] 283: An account of the reigns of many kings born in the lineage of King Bhoja; the topic of the Lord's incarnation for the increase of the Kali [age]; the performance of austerities by an Ābhīra woman named Vratapā who desired to have the Lord as her son; and the marriage of the Ābhīra woman Vratapā with King Suman; the birth from her of two sons, Deśarāja and Vatsarāja; their making of an alliance with Tālana, lord of Vanarasa, after he was defeated in battle; an account of their journey to test Jayacandra: 31 verses.
5 [page] 284: An account of the origin of Jayacandra and Pṛthvīrāja, followed by their sovereignty over equal halves of the Āryan land, and an account of their mutual enmity: 38 verses.

9 [page] 287: An account of the marriages of Deśarāja and Vatsarāja; an account of the stories of the partial incarnations of Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, Dharma, and the rest: 49 verses.

3.3.m:
16 [page] 297: An account of the marriage of Balakhāni when the part of Kṛṣṇa was seventeen years of age; in that connection, an account of the crisis of Balakhāni and his deliverance from it: 74 verses.
17 [page] 299: An account of Pṛthvīrāja obtaining seven sons who were parts of the Kauravas; an account of the marriage of Brahmānanda: 69 verses.
18 [page] 300: After the account of Padminī was told to Indula by swans, his going to Siṃhala for her sake, followed by an account of the battle and other events; in that battle, an account of the defeat of the army of Balakhāni: 29 verses.
19 [page] 301: An account of the marriage of Indula with Padminī; an account of the birth of Padminī: 58 verses.
20 [page] 302: An account of the grace of Skanda upon Mayūradhvaja, son of King Balavardhana residing in the country of Pañcāla, and an account of the grace of Varuṇa upon his brother Lahara; an account of the marriage of Sukhakhāni: 52 verses.
21 [page] 303: An account of the marriage of the part of Kṛṣṇa with Puṣpavatī, daughter of King Mayūradhvaja residing in the country of Sindhu: 105 verses.

24 310 pṛdhvīrājāgre candrabhaṭṭena bhāṣāgraṃthavarṇanam pṛthvīrājena mahāvatyāṃ kuṃdanamalasya dautyena preṣaṇam nṛpāṇāṃ parasparajayaparājayādivividhavṛttāntavarṇanam ślo, 106
25 312 dākṣiṇātyabindugaḍhasthaśāradānandanabhūpakanyāyāḥ svayaṃvaravṛttāntavarṇanam ślo. 61

3.3.d:

23 307 चित्ररेखया सहेन्दुलस्य विवाहवृत्तान्तवर्णनम् श्लो। 140
24 310 पृध्वीराजाग्रे चन्द्रभट्टेन भाषाग्रंथवर्णनम् पृथ्वीराजेन महावत्यां कुंदनमलस्य दौत्येन प्रेषणम् नृपाणां परस्परजयपराजयादिविविधवृत्तान्तवर्णनम् श्लो, 106
25 312 दाक्षिणात्यबिन्दुगढस्थशारदानन्दनभूपकन्यायाः स्वयंवरवृत्तान्तवर्णनम् श्लो। 61
26 313 महावत्यां युद्धवृत्तांतवर्णनम् श्लो, 106

3.3.m:
22 [page] 305: In the conversation between the part of Kṛṣṇa and Puṣpavatī, an account of their previous births; an account of the part of Kṛṣṇa going to the abode of his sister Candrāvalī and meeting her; an account of the battle there when slander was committed by the deceitful king: 70 verses.
23 [page] 307: An account of the marriage of Indula with Citrarekhā: 140 verses.
24 [page] 310: Before Pṛthvīrāja, the recitation of a work in the vernacular by the bard Candra; the sending of Kundanamala on an embassy to Mahāvatī by Pṛthvīrāja; an account of the various victories, defeats, and so forth of the kings among one another: 106 verses.
25 [page] 312: An account of the self-choice of the daughter of King Śāradānandana residing in southern Bindugaḍha: 61 verses.
26 [page] 313: An account of the battle at Mahāvatī: 106 verses.
27 [page] 315: An account of the battle in the country of Kaccha: 79 verses.
28 [page] 317: An account of the divisions of the Purāṇas and their teachers following the conversation and encounter of the part of Kṛṣṇa with a courtesan named Śobhā; an account of the deliverance of the part of Kṛṣṇa when led away by the courtesan Śobhā: 80 verses.

3.3.s:

3.3.d:
29 319 किंनरीकन्योत्पत्तिवृत्तान्तवर्णनम् बौद्धराज्य-चीनराज्य श्यामराजस्थैः सह युद्धवृत्तान्तवर्णनम् श्लो। 59

3.3.m:
29 [page] 319: An account of the birth of the maiden who was a Kinnarī; an account of the battle against those who dwelled in the Buddhist kingdom, the kingdom of Cīna, and the kingdom of Śyāma: 59 verses.
30 [page] 320: An account of the battle fought for the fetching of Lakṣaṇā and Padminī: 94 verses.
31 [page] 322: The plunging of the part of Kṛṣṇa into a crisis by the wives of his brothers-in-law; an account of the marriage of the part of Kṛṣṇa with the wives of his brothers-in-law and other matters; the subduing of the yakṣa who afflicted Prabhāvatī, daughter of King Mūladeva residing in Gurjara, and her husband; an account of the marriage with Madanāvatī, daughter of the king of Kekaya residing in Kāśmīra; an account of the marriage with Suvelā, daughter of King Nāgavarma residing in the country of Puṇḍra; an account of the marriage with Kāntimatī, daughter of the king of Madra; an account of the arrival toward Dehalī of Sahoda, the mleccha king; an account of the arrival of the mlecchas into the Āryan country and other matters: 186 verses.

3.3.s: 32 326 candravaṃśīyādisarvanṛpāṇāmaṃtimamahāghorasaṃgrāmaḥ, tatra prāyaḥ sarvanṛpāṇāṃ kṣayavṛttā ntavarṇanam pṛdhvīrājamṛtyuvidvanmālāharaṇavṛttāntavarṇanam mlecchena sahoḍḍīnena dehalyāṃ svadūtasya kutukoḍḍīnasya sthāpanavarṇanam ślo, 347
3.3.d: 32 326 चन्द्रवंशीयादिसर्वनृपाणामंतिममहाघोरसंग्रामः, तत्र प्रायः सर्वनृपाणां क्षयवृत्ता न्तवर्णनम् पृध्वीराजमृत्युविद्वन्मालाहरणवृत्तान्तवर्णनम् म्लेच्छेन सहोड्डीनेन देहल्यां स्वदूतस्य कुतुकोड्डीनस्य स्थापनवर्णनम् श्लो, 347
3.3.m: 32 [fol.] 326. Account of the final terrible battle of all the kings of the Lunar dynasty and others; account of the destruction of almost all kings there; account of the death of Pṛthvīrāja and the abduction of Vidvanmālā; account of the installation of his envoy Kutukoḍḍīna in Delhi by the mleccha Sahoḍḍīna. Verses: 347.
